Oxley Camera Club Bulletin: Member Spotlight
Anjali Mehta
Each month, this column introduces a club member whose recent work deserves attention. This month we turn to Anjali Mehta, who entered a photograph in a judged show this year for the first time.
Anjali joined the club only last year, though she has photographed birds and trees on weekend walks for about three years.
Choosing one image for the Grantham Arts Center's autumn show was the hardest part. For six weeks, she brought a folder of possible prints to Print Review, the weekly session in which members comment on one another's work. Their remarks helped her narrow twenty pictures down to one, a heron standing in morning fog, which the judges accepted. It hangs at the center until November 30, and prizes will be announced at the closing reception.
Anjali is already looking ahead. After three years of birds and trees, she wants her next pictures to have faces in them, and Henrik Maas, who has photographed weddings for twenty years, has offered to spend Saturday mornings sharing what he knows.
Doreen Clay, Bulletin Editor
----------------------

Doreen Clay, Bulletin Editor

November 4

Dear Ms. Clay,

Please consider printing this letter in the bulletin. Like several members this year, I entered the Grantham Arts Center's autumn show for the first time, although I have belonged to the club for five years. When the center called at the end of the summer to say that my picture of fishing boats at dawn would hang in its main hall until the end of November, I could hardly believe it. Before the show opened, I had it framed at a local shop.

Much of the credit belongs to our weekly evening meetings. Through the summer, I brought new prints almost every week, and other members told me honestly which ones held their attention. The center will accept entries for its spring show until January 12. If you are thinking of entering, start bringing your work to those meetings now, while there is still time to act on what you hear.

Sincerely,
Gwen Sorensen

Lorimer Film Week Returns in November
By Joel Abernathy, Staff Reporter
LORIMER (October 27) — Lorimer Film Week, which has run for seven days every year since it began in 2012, returns from November 6 to November 12. For years, local theater managers said the December holidays brought in their biggest audiences. They now say the festival draws even larger crowds.
Filmgoers can choose from three ticket options. A single ticket, which cost $12 last year, is now $9 and admits one person to one screening. A $25 day pass covers any number of films on one day, and an $80 festival pass is good for all seven days. Single tickets can be used at every participating cinema, but passes are not accepted everywhere, so filmgoers should check the online schedule before buying one.
The festival was started by the Lorimer Film Society at three downtown theaters. Each year since then, more titles have been added to the program. This year, eleven cinemas will screen 64 films, about half of them by first-time directors.
Schedules for every participating cinema are posted at www.lorimerfilmweek.org.

A Gardener's First Book
Moira Doyle turns years of hands-on work into a practical guide
By Judith Lang
Ms. Doyle trained far from home. After studying design in the Netherlands, she spent three years caring for the flower beds of a large public park in Amsterdam, where she learned to plan beds that stay colorful all year.
A move to Canada followed. There, a newspaper editor who admired her gardens asked her to write a weekly advice column, and her readers' questions slowly shaped the chapters of
Planting for Every Season
.
Now back in New Zealand, where she grew up, Ms. Doyle runs Stonebridge Garden Center. Starting in April, she will also lead hands-on workshops there for readers who want to try the methods in her book.
Home Garden Monthly, London | March issue
----------------------
To: Luke Sutter
From: Judith Lang
Date: March 18
Subject: Stonebridge visit: thank you
Luke,
Thank you for reserving me a place at one of Moira Doyle's first workshops. Watching her teach should make a good follow-up to the profile.
The timing is ideal, as I will already be in her home country next month. The Southern Garden Writers Forum has invited me to give its opening speech, so the visit adds just one day to my trip. Any date after the forum ends on April 16 suits me.
Warm regards,
Judith Lang
Staff Writer, Home Garden Monthly
----------------------

From:

Thank you for your message. Ms. Doyle, who has been showing the March profile in Home Garden Monthly to many of our visitors, is glad that your writer can join her workshop on Friday, April 17.

Kind regards,
Megan Hurley
Workshop Coordinator, Stonebridge Garden Center
